welcome.title: Welcome to Lunar Outpost Aquarius
storySentences: Four astronauts live at Shackleton Crater on the Moon.
A 72-hour solar storm is coming, and the Sun will hide behind the ridge for 46 hours.
You must balance power, air, water, food, and the radiation shield to keep everyone safe.

tutorial.tradeOffAfter: After: Shield 450 L (~90% SAFE) | Tank 70 L (<200 L warns plants/O2!)
tutorial.step1: In space, every resource is connected! Pumping water into the shelter walls blocks deadly solar radiation, but takes water away from the plants and oxygen maker.
tutorial.step2: Try 1 Move Now: Click 'Pump 450 L to Shield Wall' below and watch both the Water & Plants and Radiation Shield meters at the bottom change together!
tutorial.step3: Look at the trade-off! Radiation Shield jumped to SAFE (~90% blocked), while Tank Water dropped to 70 L (under 200 L starves plants!). During the dark eclipse, you'll also dim Plant Lights to 25% to save Battery.

power.label: Power (Battery)
power.jargon: kWh = stored electricity for heaters, air pumps, and plant lights.

air.label: Air (O2 & CO2)
air.jargon: mmHg = breathed-out CO2 gas pressure; keep under 4.0 so crew thinks clearly.

waterFood.label: Water & Plants
waterFood.jargon: Keep >= 200 L in main tank or plants & oxygen makers dry out.

shield.label: Radiation Shield
shield.jargon: mSv/h = radiation speed; water walls block solar protons.

debrief.workedLeak: Sealed water leak with V-2 Methane Pyrolysis.
debrief.workedShield: Blocked Carrington storm with shelter water wall.
debrief.workedBattery: Kept battery charged through 46h crater shadow eclipse.
debrief.workedAir: Kept CO2 under toxic limit with Mailbox scrubber.
debrief.workedPlants: Kept space garden and tank water alive.
debrief.failedLeak: Forgot V-2 Methane Pyrolysis — vented water.

labels.whyItMatters: Why it matters for the crew

bvad_metabolism.whatItIs: NASA's list of how much air, water, and food one astronaut needs each day.
bvad_metabolism.whyItMatters: Four crew breathe in about 0.140 kg of oxygen and breathe out about 0.167 kg of CO2 every hour.
bvad_metabolism.whatYouCanDo: Match the air and food systems to these numbers so nobody runs out.

bvad_electrolysis_sabatier.whatItIs: Ways to split water into oxygen and hydrogen, and to turn CO2 into methane.
bvad_electrolysis_sabatier.whyItMatters: Splitting water takes 4.5 kWh of power per kg of oxygen. If methane is vented, about 0.068 L of water leaves the base every hour.
bvad_electrolysis_sabatier.whatYouCanDo: Turn ON the V-2 Methane Pyrolysis loop so the hydrogen and water are saved.

aug1972_spe_flux.whatItIs: A huge solar storm in August 1972 sent harmful space particles toward the Moon.
aug1972_spe_flux.whyItMatters: At its peak it reached 62,000 pfu, and without shielding the dose rate hit 142.0 mSv/hr.
aug1972_spe_flux.whatYouCanDo: Get behind the water wall and keep the crew In Shelter.

crater_oltaris_waterwall.whatItIs: Tests show that water is good at blocking space radiation.
crater_oltaris_waterwall.whyItMatters: A 500 L water jacket on a 25 m^2 wall cuts the storm dose by about 90%.
crater_oltaris_waterwall.whatYouCanDo: Fill the Water Shield (450 L) before the storm peak arrives.

lola_shackleton_eclipse.whatItIs: The ridge around Shackleton Crater blocks the low Sun and creates a long shadow.
lola_shackleton_eclipse.whyItMatters: The shadow lasts 46 hours, from Hour 12 to Hour 58, and the ground gets much colder, from 220 K down to 42 K.
lola_shackleton_eclipse.whatYouCanDo: Set Plant Lights to 25% so the battery lasts through the dark.

veggie_hydroponics.whatItIs: Plants grown in water and light help clean the air and make food.
veggie_hydroponics.whyItMatters: A full 12 m^2 plant bay uses 14.0 kW of light and scrubs 0.095 kg of CO2 while making 0.070 kg of O2 each hour.
veggie_hydroponics.whatYouCanDo: Keep the tank water above 200 L so the plants stay alive.

nasa_std_3001.whatItIs: NASA's safety rules for how much CO2 and radiation a crew can handle.
nasa_std_3001.whyItMatters: CO2 at 4.0 mmHg or more makes thinking hard, and 75 mSv or more of radiation means the mission must stop.
nasa_std_3001.whatYouCanDo: Turn ON Mailbox Air Boost and keep the crew In Shelter to stay under these limits.
